correctness.rationale: The claim is a finite exhaustive theorem on KG(5,2): 10 vertices, 15 edges and all 60 non-induced simple four-vertex paths. Both programs independently generate these objects. Every invalid partial six-colour map has a permanent monochromatic edge or alternating two-colour four-path, so exhaustive prefix-pruning does not omit any valid assignment. C++ verifies all 341280 valid named six-palette maps, all one-position substitutions, the full degree spectrum and degree sum 2188800; in the five-name subgraph every one of 7680 valid maps has degree zero. Python exhausts all 115975 vertex set partitions, obtains exactly 64 admissible five-block and 410 six-block partitions, and independently verifies corresponding named palette counts, degrees and 11 vertex-symmetry orbits. C++ full NAMED-state BFS on each of the 11 ground-set-and-colour-renaming orbit representatives visits all 341280 states, producing eccentricities 14 and 15 with weighted multiplicities 21600 and 319680. The automorphisms preserve every allowed recolouring; the 11 full BFS traversals cover all source orbits, certifying radius14 and diameter15. Programs and actual assertion-passing outputs are embedded in the same finding. The independent partition code does not independently recompute all BFS distances, a stated reproducibility limitation.

value.rationale: Star-colouring imposes a genuine strengthening of proper-colouring locality; the basic star-chromatic number alone gives no information about reachability. The theorem exhibits a sharp, counterintuitive state-space transition on the canonical cubic Petersen graph: all 7680 optimal five-name states frozen but a sixth available name connects 341280 states. Exact reconfiguration diameter/radius and state/degree census quantify this local mobility and give a nontrivial reproducible benchmark for constrained graph-colouring reconfiguration. The motivation is a natural optimality-vs-mobility gap, not an arbitrary numerical slice; finite scope is acknowledged.
